summary: Feed s182_triple to APM is degraded: 53.3% of TCP sessions are one-way, 9.1% packets are duplicates, and 1ms microbursts hit 15.34 Gbps on a 10 Gbps APM port (153% capacity). APM will see incomplete transactions and inflated retransmissions while dropping packets during bursts.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is not aggregating both directions of flows to the same tool port. 270 of 507 TCP sessions (53.3%) show only one direction, typical of asymmetric routing or ECMP/SPAN aggregation where client->server and server->client take different paths and are hashed to different outputs without symmetric aggregation.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM needs_both_directions=true to correlate requests and responses for latency, response time and TCP handshake analysis. With one-way traffic APM creates incomplete flows, cannot measure server response time, misses errors, and generates false timeout/retransmission alerts.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate/bond both directions using symmetric hashing so each bidirectional flow is delivered to the same APM port, restoring complete request-response visibility required for APM.

findings.root_cause: Microburst of 15.34 Gbps in a 1ms interval exceeds the APM's 10 Gbps port capacity by 53% (153% of capacity). Broker is forwarding full aggregate without load-balancing or shaping, overrunning the tool's ingress buffer.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM will randomly drop packets during bursts, losing transactions, creating gaps in application performance metrics, and causing incomplete flow records and false performance degradation alerts.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute flows across 2+ APM ports with symmetric 5-tuple hashing to keep per-port utilization under 80% while keeping both directions of each flow together, preventing burst drops.

findings.root_cause: 9.1% duplicate packets (570 of 6265) indicates overlapping SPAN/mirror sources or double-tapped links being aggregated without deduplication on the packet broker, forwarding the same packet twice.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM wastes ~9% capacity processing redundant packets and will miscount duplicates as TCP retransmissions, inflating throughput, transaction counts and skewing latency/retransmission metrics.

recommended_fix.why: Enable broker deduplication to drop identical packets seen within a short time window before forwarding to APM, eliminating false retransmissions and freeing tool capacity.
